title: C182 — Fuel injector 2 connector reference
introduction:
A fuel injector is an electrically controlled valve that meters fuel into the engine. I use this reference as the address book for its electrical connection: the identity table names the connector, the drawing locates its cavity labels, and the circuit table explains each connection's assigned job.

Start with the identity table, then match a cavity label in the drawing to the Cavity column below. Read across that row to keep its circuit, color, gauge, function and terminal entry together. The injector-driver and fuse-or-circuit-breaker power descriptions distinguish the circuit roles; they do not demonstrate that the injector is operating correctly.

This guide covers reading the reference. Engine applicability, physical viewing direction, gauge convention and the meanings of Size and Used are unspecified here. Access, probing, wire selection, testing and replacement require separate applicable instructions.

edits.why: I use the latch-shaped feature at the top of the drawing to keep the pictured layout straight: the cavities are stacked vertically beneath it. That describes the illustration's arrangement, without establishing which side of the physical connector to view. The accompanying Fpn entry can be cross-checked against Hard Shell in the identity table.

The cavity label joins the drawing to its table row; the circuit identifier then distinguishes that electrical path. Color and Gauge describe the same row, while Function identifies the injector-driver or fuse-or-circuit-breaker power role. I keep the complete function wording, including its suffix, without treating it as a voltage measurement or a test instruction. A blank Qualifier supplies no additional condition.

A pigtail is the connector with attached wire leads. I read Number alongside Kit List, then distinguish the Service Part entry from Engineering Shell and the pin table's Terminal Part Number. These identify different service items. The pigtail and circuit tables describe separate records; their Gauge entries alone do not establish replacement-wire suitability or a splice method.

editorialRevision.scope: Replace fused shorthand with literal fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternative. All action/table/figure content unchanged.
